+title: Replay the child associations on session/resume with replayFrom start
+---
+## What
+v2 has no `session/load`. `session/resume` with `replayFrom: {type: "start"}` replays the history. Add the children to that replay.
+
+The Router already records the parent link (`SessionRecord.agentSpawn.parentSessionId`) and restores the tree (`SessionTreeRestoration`, `TranscriptTree.children(of:)`). In `Sources/FoundationModelsACPAgent/Agent/SessionResume.swift` and `SessionHistory.swift`:
+- Read the child records of the resumed session from the restored tree.
+- Replay `subagent_update` for each child, the full ancestor chain, parent before child, before any child event.
+- Replay child messages under the child id, best effort. Never guess a parent and never invent an id: a child with an unknown parent stays unexposed.
+- Replay must not send a permission request again.
+- Give each replayed child the NEW live id rule: a child id restored from disk keeps its recorded id (the table of the first task must accept a restored id).
+- Child capabilities from before the resume do not carry over: the replay sends `capabilities` fresh (idle children get none that they cannot honor).
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+- [ ] Resume of a session that had a nested run replays parent first, then child, then grandchild.
+- [ ] No child event comes before its `subagent_update`.
+- [ ] A child with an unknown parent is not sent.
+- [ ] No permission request is sent during the replay.
+
+## Tests
+- [ ] `Tests/FoundationModelsACPAgentTests/SubagentReplayTests.swift`: record a session with a nested run with the stub model, resume, check the order of the wire messages.
+- [ ] Run `swift test --filter SubagentReplayTests`. All pass.
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd` — write failing tests first, then implement to make them pass. #subagents
\ No newline at end of file

 ## What
-v2 has no `session/load`. `session/resume` with `replayFrom: {type: "start"}` replays the history. Add the nested tree to that replay, following the ACP subagents RFD (see the rule list below). The sessions are restored and registered by the cold resume task (a dependency); this task sends the history of the tree on the wire.
+v2 has no `session/load`. `session/resume` with `replayFrom: {type: "start"}` replays the history. Add the children to that replay.

-Rules (ACP "Subagent Sessions" RFD):
-- The agent announces the full ancestor chain, parent before child, with `subagent_update`, before any child traffic. A missing intermediate ancestor is still announced (identity, not a live runtime). Never guess a parent; never invent an id.
-- Replayed child updates keep their original session ids, parentage and per-session order. All history selected for the replay is sent BEFORE the response. The response completes the best-effort child replay.
-- Replay must not reissue permission, elicitation or other agent-to-client requests.
-- Current child state and capability snapshots are NOT part of the replay: they come after the response (child sync task).
-- The child `session_message` history is replayed under the right transcript when the `session_message` wire type exists.
-
-Where: `Sources/FoundationModelsACPAgent/Agent/SessionResume.swift` (`replayHistory`) and `SessionHistory.swift` (`replayUpdates`). Each child has its own retained history (`retainedHistory` of its session entry); replay each under its own id.
+The Router already records the parent link (`SessionRecord.agentSpawn.parentSessionId`) and restores the tree (`SessionTreeRestoration`, `TranscriptTree.children(of:)`). In `Sources/FoundationModelsACPAgent/Agent/SessionResume.swift` and `SessionHistory.swift`:
+- Read the child records of the resumed session from the restored tree.
+- Replay `subagent_update` for each child, the full ancestor chain, parent before child, before any child event.
+- Replay child messages under the child id, best effort. Never guess a parent and never invent an id: a child with an unknown parent stays unexposed.
+- Replay must not send a permission request again.
+- Give each replayed child the NEW live id rule: a child id restored from disk keeps its recorded id (the table of the first task must accept a restored id).
+- Child capabilities from before the resume do not carry over: the replay sends `capabilities` fresh (idle children get none that they cannot honor).

 ## Acceptance Criteria
-- [ ] A resume with `replayFrom: start` of a root with a nested run (depth 3) sends: announcements parent first, then the history of each session under its own id, all before the response.
+- [ ] Resume of a session that had a nested run replays parent first, then child, then grandchild.
 - [ ] No child event comes before its `subagent_update`.
-- [ ] No permission or elicitation request is sent during the replay.
-- [ ] No child current-state snapshot is sent before the response.
-- [ ] A resume with no `replayFrom` sends no history.
+- [ ] A child with an unknown parent is not sent.
+- [ ] No permission request is sent during the replay.
